first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence links simpler, shorter onboarding to durable activation and faster time-to-value. This addresses two current weaknesses without using price cuts that may attract lower-value cohorts. Verify memory_86 to assess segment fit, experiment design, and whether gains extended beyond early adoption toward qualified revenue. Long-term revenue impact remains uncertain, so use a controlled experiment rather than a broad rollout.

final.rationale: Run a standard controlled experiment shortening the onboarding flow. The verified source showed completion +13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, directly addressing the current declines in onboarding completion and activation while supporting sustainability. Memory_31 independently reinforces the activation benefit of reducing signup friction. Qualified-revenue impact was not directly measured, so the experiment should track downstream account qualification, conversion, retention, and revenue rather than assume early-funnel gains will fully translate.
